sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Georgia, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Friday, October 23Passed

Your application must be received by your county election office 11 days before the election: Friday, October 23, 2026. Requests could be made starting 78 days before the election. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your county election office must receive your ballot by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A postmark is not enough for voters inside the country. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Friday, October 30, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Georgia’s own site

At school away from home, in Georgia or in another state? What Georgia says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Any registered Georgia voter can ask for an absentee ballot, but you must ask for one each time; the state does not mail ballots to everyone. (The state's application form lets voters who are 65 or older, have a physical disability, or are military or overseas tick a box to get ballots for the rest of the election cycle.) (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Use the Secretary of State's absentee request portal. You fill in the form online, then print it, sign it by hand in ink, and upload a photo or scan of the signed form (and a copy of your ID if you are not registered with a Georgia driver's license or state ID card). Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Print the state's application, fill it in, sign it by hand in ink, and mail it to your county board of registrars. You can also send the signed form to your county by email (as an attachment) or by fax. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Hand the signed application to your county board of registrars' office and bring an accepted photo ID. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it in the return envelope so it arrives by 7 p.m. on Election Day. Allow extra time for the mail. (official page)
  • Drop box. Every county has at least one drop box. Drop boxes are indoors and open only during their operating hours; in Cobb County, for one, the county's page lists six drop boxes open from October 13 through Friday, October 30, 2026. Ask your county election office where its drop boxes are and when they close. (official page)
  • In person. Hand it in at your county election office. Only you, or your mother, father, grandparent, aunt, uncle, brother, sister, spouse, son, daughter, niece, nephew, grandchild, son-in-law, daughter-in-law, mother-in-law, father-in-law, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, or someone who lives in your household, may mail or deliver your ballot. (official page)

What the envelope needs

No witness is needed. On the application, give your date of birth AND your Georgia driver's license or state ID card number; if you have neither, include a copy of another accepted ID (such as a U.S. passport, a military ID, a utility bill or bank statement showing your name and address). On the return envelope, sign the oath in ink, print your name, write your date of birth, and give your Georgia driver's license or ID number or the last four digits of your Social Security number; if you have none of these, put a copy of an accepted ID in the envelope. Sign it yourself: signing for another voter is against the law. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Georgia’s own site

Log in to the Georgia My Voter Page and look for "Absentee Ballot Request Information" to see whether your ballot was received and accepted. (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Tuesday, October 13, 2026 to Friday, October 30, 2026.

Early voting in person runs Tuesday, October 13 through Friday, October 30, 2026, including Saturday, October 17 and Saturday, October 24; some places may also open on Sunday, October 18 and Sunday, October 25. You may vote at any early voting place in your county. Hours and places are set by your county. (official page)

Students

At school in Georgia, away from home

The state's pages that we could read do not speak to students separately. The state's absentee application lets you give a temporary mailing address for your ballot if you are temporarily living outside the county where you are registered; that address must be in a different county. The application also says that if you no longer live at the address where you are registered, you should contact your county election office before you apply. We could not read the state's residence law (Georgia's code is not posted on a state website we could reach), and the Secretary of State's own website did not answer our request. (official page)

At school in another state, with Georgia as home

The state's pages that we could read do not speak to students separately. On the absentee application, a voter temporarily living outside their county, including outside Georgia, can give a temporary mailing address where the ballot will be sent. A close relative can also apply for a voter who is temporarily living outside the county. You must still be eligible to vote in the county where you are registered. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military and overseas voters use the Federal Post Card Application to register and ask for a ballot (by mail, email or fax); it must be received by Friday, October 23, 2026, and you can ask to get your ballot by email. A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Election Day, November 3, and received within three days after (by Friday, November 6, 2026). Georgia also sends an instant runoff ballot to these voters with the November ballot, for any runoff on December 1, 2026. If your ballot has not come, you can use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot. (federal guide)

Georgia in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The request deadline is this Friday, October 23, 2026. A ballot mailed after that has little time to travel both ways; you can also vote early in person through October 30 or at your polling place on Election Day.
  • Once you return your absentee ballot, you have voted and cannot vote again in person. If your requested ballot never came, you can vote in person after signing a statement that you are voting only once.
  • If there is a problem with your ballot envelope (most often a missing signature), your county will contact you with a way to fix it.

How this was checked

  • The Secretary of State's website (sos.ga.gov) answered our request with a check for human visitors, which we did not try to get past. The rules above come from Georgia.gov, the Secretary of State's own forms, county election offices and the Federal Voting Assistance Program. The return instructions come from a county copy of the state's instruction sheet (form ABI-MO-21, 2022); the sheet in your ballot package is the one to follow.
Where this comes from: 7 pages of Georgia’s election office, its laws and the federal guide
  1. Vote by Absentee Ballot (last updated June 2026), Georgia.gov (State of Georgia), with the Secretary of State (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  2. Application for Georgia Official Absentee Ballot (form APP-21), Georgia Secretary of State (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  3. Last Day to Request Absentee Ballots for General Election (October 23, 2026), Georgia.gov (State of Georgia) (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  4. Instructions for marking and returning an official absentee ballot (form ABI-MO-21), Gwinnett County Voter Registrations and Elections (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  5. General Election Early Voting, October 13 to 30, 2026 (and the state's events list), Georgia.gov (State of Georgia) (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  6. Voting Assistance Guide: Georgia (updated October 1, 2026), Federal Voting Assistance Program (federal guide; read October 21, 2026)
  7. Absentee Voting, Cobb County Board of Elections and Registration (official page; read October 21, 2026)

Checked October 21, 2026. Rules and dates can change: Georgia’s election office, and your county or local election office, have the final word.
